say.en: A clipper cuts a wave; a clamper moves it. With just a capacitor and a diode, a sine wave centred on zero can be lifted so that it sits entirely above zero. In this lesson: Explain the working of a positive and a negative clamper.
Find the output levels with an ideal and a silicon diode.
State the RC condition and uses.

body.en: A clamper adds a DC level to an AC signal without changing its shape. It has a capacitor in series and a diode across the output (with a resistor or load across it). In a *positive* clamper, during the negative peak the diode conducts and C charges to $V_m$. Then the diode stays off and C acts as a battery of $V_m$ in series with the input, so $v_o = v_i + V_m$: the output swings from 0 to $+2V_m$. Reversing the diode gives a negative clamper with output from 0 to $-2V_m$. Clampers are also called DC restorers.

narration.en: In a positive clamper the capacitor charges to Vm through the diode, then adds Vm to the input, so the output runs from zero to two Vm.
narration.kn: ಧನಾತ್ಮಕ ಕ್ಲ್ಯಾಂಪರ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಧಾರಕ ಡಯೋಡ್ ಮೂಲಕ Vm ಗೆ ಆವೇಶಗೊಂಡು ಇನ್‌ಪುಟ್‌ಗೆ Vm ಸೇರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ; ಔಟ್‌ಪುಟ್ 0 ಯಿಂದ 2Vm ವರೆಗೆ.

narration.en: Play. In a positive clamper the diode conducts at the first negative peak and charges C to about Vm − 0.7 V; after that the diode is off and the whole wave is lifted by that DC level, from −0.7 V to about 2Vm. If RL C is not much longer than the period, C leaks between peaks and the wave sags.

body.en: With a silicon diode, C charges only to $V_m - 0.7$ V, so a positive clamper gives an output from −0.7 V to $2V_m - 0.7$ V. The time constant $R_LC$ must be much larger (at least about 5 to 10 times) than the period of the input so that C hardly discharges between peaks. A battery in series with the diode (biased clamper) clamps the wave at any chosen level. Uses: restoring the DC level of video signals in TV receivers, and voltage multipliers.

points.en: Si diode: output from −0.7 V to 2Vm − 0.7 V
Biased clamper: clamp at any level
Uses: TV DC restorer, voltage multipliers

problem.en: A positive clamper with a silicon diode receives a 10 V peak sine wave. Find the output range and its DC level.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. A positive clamper with a silicon diode receives a 10 V peak sine wave. Find the output range and its DC level.

say.en: Let us work this out together. A positive clamper with a silicon diode receives a 10 volts peak sine wave. Find the output range and its DC level.
C charges to Vm minus 0.7 equals 9.3 volts.
vo equals vi plus 9.3 volts.
Minimum: minus 10 plus 9.3 equals minus 0.7 volts; maximum: 10 plus 9.3 equals 19.3 volts.
DC average level = plus 9.3 volts.
So the answer is minus 0.7 volts to plus 19.3 volts.

problem.en: A clamper works at 1 kHz with RL = 100 kΩ. Choose C so that RLC is at least 10 times the period.

steps.en: Choosing C = 1 µF gives RLC = 100 ms, safely large.

answer.en: C ≥ 0.1 µF (1 µF is a safe choice)

narration.en: Let us work this out together. A clamper works at 1 kHz with RL = 100 kΩ. Choose C so that RLC is at least 10 times the period.

say.en: Let us work this out together. A clamper works at 1 kilohertz with RL equals 100 k ohms. Choose C so that RLC is at least 10 times the period.
T equals 1 over 1000 equals 1 millisecond, so RLC is greater than or equal to 10 milliseconds.
C is greater than or equal to 10 ms over 100 k ohms equals 0.1 microfarads.
Choosing C equals 1 microfarad gives RLC equals 100 milliseconds, safely large.
So the answer is C is greater than or equal to 0.1 microfarads (1 microfarad is a safe choice).
